content: Plug the wide connector of the branched head cable into the Nextruder-labeled slot and leave the narrow connector unplugged  and route it back through the left opening. Plug the connector of the cable with just a single connector in the MMU-labeled slot.
This step shows X-Y motors plugged in, if you're following Gen2 upgrade as well they don't say to plug them back in up to this point.. Kind of annoying, hopefully I get them in the correct spots
My cable sleeve must be much shorter, doesn't go as far as the picture depicts

replies.content: Same for me. I guess functionally does not matter.

content: I feel like this is the ideal time to re-connect the X and Y connectors if you are also doing the Core One + Gen 2 upgrade since you are about to use and cut the zip ties.

replies.content: They do that earlier in the combined guide: https://help.prusa3d.com/article/assemblling-the-prusa-indx-core-one-with-the-gen-2-upgrade_1147602#removing-old-expansion-joints. However, I also missed it as I don't think I saw a reference in this guide.

From what I see, they don't have you re-connect the X and Y motor to the buddy board til much later in the combined guide. So, I think Matt is right, this may be a better time to plug in the X and Y motors back in.
